## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly grounded in the integral theorem at [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235].
- claim-2: Correctly distinguishes the source-stated remark from a formally stated right-family theorem. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
- claim-3: Adequately supports the integral ring involution and conjugation invariance of Littlewood–Richardson coefficients. The induced quotient isomorphism follows because conjugation exchanges partitions outside \(q^r\) with those outside \(r^q\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-491]
- claim-4: The argument is valid. The accepted admissibility certificate ensures that \(v^\vee\) is bigrassmannian with parameters \((j,i,a,b)\). The quotient isomorphism sends the original right-adjoined family bijectively to the lower-adjoined family for \(v^\vee\). Any relation placing one right-family member in the ideal generated by the others would therefore contradict claim-1 for \(v^\vee\). Right-family generation is separately grounded by claim-2. The \(a=0\) singleton boundary is also covered by the accepted admissibility certificate. Thus the requested target is established as an internal consequence, not as a separately source-stated theorem.
